200.note: In 200, with China splitting into warlord states, Cao Cao, who held the Han emperor at Xu, turned on his northern rival Yuan Shao, while Septimius Severus had restored peace to Rome after the upheavals of the late 2nd century.

rome.blurb: Septimius Severus had replaced the Praetorian Guard with Danubian veterans and stationed a new legion at Albanum, 20 km away. After defeating Parthia he raised a triumphal arch in the Forum, and he also built the Septizodium.

image.file: File:Arch of Septimius Severus in Rome (1).jpg
image.caption: The Arch of Septimius Severus in the Roman Forum, raised after his Parthian victory; photo 2018.

alexandria.blurb: Egypt's grain came down the Nile to Lake Mareotis and sailed from Alexandria's Great Harbour for Rome. Clement ran the city's Catechetical School, teaching Christianity through Greek philosophy, until Septimius Severus's persecution drove him to Palestine in 202.

sources.title: Grain supply to the city of Rome - Wikipedia

image.file: File:Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, Alexandria, Egypt.jpg
image.caption: Relief of Anubis tending the dead in the Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, tombs cut in the 2nd century AD and used into the 4th; photo 2020.

carthage.blurb: Centre of Roman Africa, a breadbasket of the empire, with the seaside Baths of Antoninus, Africa's largest. Tertullian, the first theologian to write in Latin, worked here; in 203 Perpetua and Felicity were executed at games for Geta's birthday.

image.caption: Ruins of the Baths of Antoninus, built under Antoninus Pius on the shore at Carthage; photo 2014.

antioch.blurb: Rome's emperors treated it as an eastern Rome, adding colonnades, baths, a granite-paved main street and a vast circus. The usurper Pescennius Niger, beaten by Septimius Severus in 194, was captured while fleeing from Antioch.

image.file: File:Mosaic of Isiac Ceremony, from Daphne near Antioch, 2nd century AD, Hatay Archaeology Museum, Antakya, Turkey (36063955161).jpg
image.caption: Floor mosaic of a ceremony for Isis from Daphne, Antioch's garden suburb, made in the 2nd century AD; Hatay Archaeology Museum.

xian.blurb: The old Western Han capital, where Dong Zhuo forced the Han court in 190. After Dong's murder his generals Li Jue and Guo Si feuded; Emperor Xian escaped east in 195, and the court now sat at Xu.

image.caption: Site of the Front Hall of Weiyang Palace, the Han palace at Chang'an that the late Eastern Han court also used; photo 2013.

300.note: Diocletian's accession in 284 ended Rome's Crisis of the Third Century, and his Tetrarchy ruled from frontier capitals; China, reunited by the Western Jin in 280, was sliding into the civil War of the Eight Princes.

noteSources.title: Crisis of the Third Century - Wikipedia

rome.blurb: No longer where emperors lived: the four tetrarchs ruled from frontier capitals such as Milan, leaving Rome the nominal capital under its own city prefect. Even so, the Baths of Diocletian, the largest imperial baths, were rising on the Viminal.

image.caption: Cross-section reconstructing the Baths of Diocletian, built 298–306, drawn by the architect Edmond Paulin in 1880.

luoyang.blurb: Capital of the Western Jin, which had reunited China in 280. In 300 its palace turned deadly: Empress Jia had the crown prince murdered, then Sima Lun deposed her and forced her suicide, deepening the War of the Eight Princes.

sources.title: War of the Eight Princes - Wikipedia

image.caption: Western Jin pottery warrior figure in the Luoyang Museum; photo 2014.

xian.blurb: No longer a capital, Chang'an was the base of Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, in the War of the Eight Princes. In 304 his general Zhang Fang brought Emperor Hui here, and in 306 Xianbei troops sacked the city.

sources.title: War of the Eight Princes - Wikipedia
War of the Eight Princes - Wikipedia
War of the Eight Princes - Wikipedia

xuchang.blurb: Cao Cao's seat for the captive Han emperor from 196 and Cao Wei's first capital in 220, Xuchang was now a Western Jin military command. In 300 Sima Lun sent the resentful Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, to hold it.

sources.title: War of the Eight Princes - Wikipedia

yecheng.blurb: Cao Cao had rebuilt Ye after 204 in the mould of an imperial capital, adding the Bronze Bird Terrace in 210. In 299 the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, was posted here, and Xianbei troops sacked the city in 304.

sources.title: War of the Eight Princes - Wikipedia

image.caption: Site of the Bronze Bird Terrace at Ye, raised by Cao Cao in 210; photo 2025.

400.note: Northern China was split among as many as nine states in 400, with the Eastern Jin ruling the south from Jiankang; a year later Alaric's Visigoths invaded Roman Italy.

rome.blurb: Emperor Honorius held court at Milan, not Rome. In 401, as Alaric's Visigoths entered Italy, Rome's walls and gates were improved and Hadrian's Tomb became a fortress; in 410 Alaric sacked the city anyway.

image.caption: Rome's Aurelian Walls near Porta San Sebastiano, the circuit Honorius improved in 401; photo 2011.

nanjing.blurb: Capital of the Eastern Jin since 317. The regent Sima Yuanxian governed for the disabled Emperor An; late in 399 Sun En's rebels overran Yang Province and advanced on Jiankang, and soon after the warlord Huan Xuan took the city.

image.file: File:20240604 Site of Jiankang in the Oriental Metropolitan Museum.jpg
image.caption: Excavated remains of Jiankang displayed in the Oriental Metropolitan Museum, Nanjing; photo 2024.

luoyang.blurb: Sacked by the Han-Zhao in 311 and fought over ever since, the former Jin capital changed hands again in winter 399, when Yao Xing's Later Qin forces took it and the surrounding cities from the Eastern Jin.

image.file: File:20240815 Site of Luoyang City from Han to Wei Dynasty - Site of the Palace City 05.jpg
image.caption: Rammed-earth remains of the palace city at the site of Han–Wei Luoyang; photo 2024.

datong.blurb: Tuoba Gui made Pingcheng the Northern Wei capital in 398, after overrunning Later Yan, and proclaimed himself emperor in 399. He founded an imperial university here, had books gathered from across his realm, and resettled people deported from conquered lands.

sources.title: Emperor Daowu of Northern Wei - Wikipedia

image.caption: Northern Wei eave tiles with moulded inscriptions, displayed in the Datong Museum; photo 2025.

xian.blurb: Capital of the Qiang-ruled Later Qin. Yao Xing invited Confucian scholars to teach here while heavily promoting Buddhism: the monk Faxian set out from Chang'an for India in 399, and Kumarajiva reached the court in 401 to translate Sanskrit texts.

yecheng.blurb: A year-long siege in the 380s left Ye so ruined that the Later Yan ruled from Zhongshan instead. Around the new year 398 its defender Murong De abandoned it to Tuoba Gui, who briefly considered making Ye his capital.
